...COMMON RESPONDENT (BY SRI. RAHUL RAI .K., HCGP)
 THESE CRIMINAL PETITIONS ARE FILED U/S.438 CR.P.C PRAYING TO ENLARGE THE PETITIONER ON BAIL IN THE EVENT OF HIS ARREST IN CR.NO.82/2024 OF TUMAKURU TOWN P.S.,
TUMAKURU DISTRICT FOR THE OFFENCE P/U/S 420, 463, 465, 468,
471 R/W 34 OF IPC ON THE FILE OF THE PRL. CIVIL JUDGE (SR.DN)
AND C.J.M COURT TUMAKURU.

THESE CRIMINAL PETITIONS, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The petitioners - accused Nos. 4 and 5 are before this Court seeking grant of anticipatory bail in Crime No. 82/2024 of Tumakuru Town Police Station, pending on the file of the learned Principal Civil Judge (Sr.Dn) and CJM Court, Tumakuru, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 463, 465, 468, 471 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC')
respectively, on the basis of the first information lodged by the informant - Chief Administrative Officer.
2. Heard Sri. Fayaz Sab B.G, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri.
Rahul Rai K, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.
Perused the materials on record.

In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the petitioners are entitled for grant of bail under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.?"

My answer to the above point is in 'Negative' for the following:
REASONS 4.
Petitioners
being accused Nos.4 and 5 are before this Court seeking grant of anticipatory bail.

Initially, the Chief Administrative Officer of District and Sessions Court, Tumakuru, lodged the first information against accused No.2 as he stood surety to an accused in a case and from the help of the software i.e., Surety Scrutiny Management Application, it was found that he already stood as surety Sri Srinivasa vs The State Of Karnataka(S.H.O) on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98669225/
2 for the accused in another case and provided false information and committed cheating and fraud.

entities.text: Sri Srinivasa vs The State Of Karnataka(S.H.O)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, accused No.2 was arrested and as per the information given by accused No.2, accused No.1 was also apprehended.
His house was searched and it is NC: 2024:KHC:20258 stated that fake Aadhar cards pertaining to the petitioners were found.
Later, these petitioners were found absconding.

5. The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that the petitioners have nothing to do with the said fake Aadhar cards cannot be accepted at this stage, as detailed investigation is required to be undertaken by the Investigating Officer.
When such serious allegations are made of creating fake Aadhar cards of the petitioners, the petitioners are required to be subjected to interrogation.

6. Accordingly, I answer the above point in the negative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is dismissed.
